lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hi Rafael, it's Yolanda from the coaching program. Is now still a good time?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi Yolanda. Give me one second... okay, I'm here.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Great. So today I'd like to hear how the vegetables went, check how you're feeling, and pick a goal for next week. Anything you want to add?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Actually, I had a question about fruit at night.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Are you feeling okay this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Pretty good actually.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That's great to hear.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Tell me how the vegetables went this week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Some days yes, some days no. Maybe 1.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My diabetes is why I'm doing this.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You figured that out on your own.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What could you try instead?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can buy the frozen bags, that's easy.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the vegetables going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know, honestly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can probably manage three days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Does your family eat salad?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I think so. I'll set an alarm on my phone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're starting to see that small changes add up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I mean, I need this for my head too, not just my body.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want to be around and be well for the people you love.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'd like to be able to keep up with my grandkids. I wrote it on the calendar.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: This is about more than the vegetables. It's about getting your life back.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How would things be different if you kept this up?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I really want to feel like myself again. I didn't think I'd like it, but I do.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want to feel like yourself again.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Part of you is already moving, and you want to keep that going.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I know I can do it, I did it before.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Just cut out the rice. That's the easiest thing.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Easy for you to say.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Would it be okay if I shared something that's helped other people?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, please.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Beans count too, and they keep you full.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay, this week I'll really do it. I don't want to end up like my dad.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Once you decide something, you follow through.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Walking hurts my knees, so why bother.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're not sure it's worth it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What do you think the next step should be?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If I plan it the night before, I can do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're starting to see that small changes add up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I put a reminder on the fridge. My grandson thinks it's funny that I have a step counter.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Half your plate has to be vegetables. That's the rule.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You already did the hardest part, which is starting.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: This is about more than the vegetables. It's about getting your life back.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I want to get my energy back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If finding the time gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll keep some fruit cut up in the fridge.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Let me make sure I got it. This week you did it 1 out of 3 days, the hard part was finding the time, and next week you're going to add a vegetable to lunch and dinner on 5 days. Did I miss anything?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, and I'll really try this time.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay Rafael, have a good rest of your day.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: God bless you.

tags.note: Reflects openness and need for fit
Reflects preference for small, sustainable steps
Reframes goal around life, meaning added
Summary and check for missed items

flags.reason: Directive advice ('Just cut out the rice') given without permission; undermines autonomy.
'That's the rule' is a prescriptive push without permission; participant replied 'I don't know'.
Participant's fruit-at-night question was never answered or revisited.
Knee pain barrier to walking was reflected but not explored; coach moved on to goal-setting without assessing the physical limitation.

score.summary: Yolanda covered the full call structure and used good reflections and autonomy statements, especially around Rafael's diabetes and family motivation. However, she twice directed him with advice ('Just cut out the rice', 'That's the rule') and never returned to his fruit question or his knee pain.
strengths: Line 12: affirmed Rafael's own insight about why he is doing this.
Line 30 and 39: emphasized autonomy with 'It's completely your call' and 'It's your plan.'
Line 40: asked permission before sharing the beans suggestion at line 42.
Line 62: clear summary and check for missed items before closing.
coaching_tips: Replace the directive at line 37 with a question such as 'Would it help to talk through some options for rice?'
Line 54 is a rule presented as fact; ask permission first or offer it as one option.
Return to Rafael's fruit-at-night question at line 4 before closing the call.
When he said walking hurts his knees (line 45), explore it with an open question and suggest he check with his care team if pain persists.
